title: Safety and immunogenicity of a first-generation modified vaccinia virus Ankara-vectored SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate with mRNA-based booster vaccination: A phase 1 trial

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of a first-generation MVA-based SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate with an mRNA booster, addressing the need for effective vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 during the early pandemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This Phase 1 trial (NCT04569383) assessed the MVA-SARS-2-S vaccine candidate in 30 healthy, SARS-CoV-2–naive adults who received two doses of either 107 or 108 IU of the vaccine 28 days apart, followed by a 6-month follow-up.
analysis.methods: The study focused on safety and reactogenicity as primary objectives, with secondary objectives measuring S1 seroconversion rates, S-domain-specific antibodies, SARS-CoV-2-neutralizing antibodies, and spike-specific T cell responses.
analysis.main_results: MVA-SARS-2-S showed a good safety profile, with no severe or serious adverse events reported. However, immunogenicity was poor, with S1-specific seroconversion occurring in 0/15 and 3/15 participants in the 107 IU and 108 IU groups, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that while the vaccine was well tolerated, it elicited insufficient immunogenicity, highlighting the need for optimized antigen design to improve its effectiveness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that further optimization of the antigen design is necessary for the MVA-SARS-2-S vaccine to be effective, which could inform future vaccine development strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study had a small sample size and limited follow-up, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This Phase 1 trial evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of a first-generation MVA-based SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate, MVA-SARS-2-S, with an mRNA booster. The study involved 30 healthy adults who received two doses of the vaccine at 107 or 108 IU, with a 6-month follow-up. The vaccine demonstrated a good safety profile, with no severe adverse events. However, immunogenicity was poor, with only limited S1 seroconversion and neutralizing antibody responses. The authors concluded that the vaccine was well tolerated but insufficiently immunogenic, emphasizing the need for optimized antigen design. The study's small sample size and limited follow-up may limit the strength of the evidence, suggesting a moderate confidence level in the findings.

analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Although evidence in high-risk groups now prioritised for vaccination in most countries remains limited, these findings clearly demonstrate the benefits of vaccination and support current seasonal vaccination strategies.

analysis.summary_en: Methods We performed an update of our previously published systematic review and meta-analysis of vaccination and LC risk (searches between 1 January 2022 and 1 March 2024). Observational studies assessing the impact of vaccination on the risk of LC four or more weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection were included. The pooled OR of LC in vaccinated adults (any dose) versus unvaccinated was 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67–0.84; 13 studies). Although evidence in high-risk groups now prioritised for vaccination in most countries remains limited, these findings clearly demonstrate the benefits of vaccination and support current seasonal vaccination strategies. Significant associations between vaccination and lower LC odds were observed in subgroup analyses of mRNA-only vaccination and LC outcomes three or more months after infection.

title: Telehealth-related education and training: a systematic review of recent developments since the COVID-19 pandemic

analysis.scope_and_question: The pandemic showed the potential of existing telehealth to increase healthcare access but also the need for healthcare workers to be competent and skilled in delivering care through this modality.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We undertook a systematic literature review to identify telehealth-related courses developed since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and summarised study characteristics, learning objectives, and course content. Quality of articles was assessed against the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines. Two authors independently extracted data.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Articles describing telehealth-related training and education programs implemented between 2020 and 2024 were included. Of 7547 articles identified, 51 were included. Most courses were implemented in the USA (82%), mostly targeted to undergraduate students (51%), and the number of articles per year increased over time. Content included basic knowledge and skills in telehealth, patient safety, and ethics, with learning objectives often on technology and communication.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Most courses were developed by universities (53%), sometimes in collaboration with health services, and content was primarily applicable across multiple specialties. Participants nearly always evaluated the courses (90%). Only four programs included all AAMC telehealth competencies. Courses generally covered telehealth communication competencies in detail, but more content on the ethical and legal requirements, billing, physical examination, patient education, and eligibility for telehealth is required.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: For efficient resource use, standardised training can be applied across disciplines with addition of site or speciality-specific modules.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines the development of telehealth-related education and training programs since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. The review identified 51 articles describing such programs, primarily targeting undergraduate students in the USA. Most courses focused on basic telehealth knowledge, technology, and communication skills, but there was a notable lack of experiential learning and coverage of ethical, legal, billing, and eligibility aspects. The findings suggest that while telehealth education has expanded, there is a need for more comprehensive curricula that address broader competencies. Standardized training across disciplines with specialized modules is recommended to optimize resource use.

The study used a nested case-control design, comparing neutralizing antibody titers between cases and matched controls. The findings suggest that natural immunity from recent infections may offer stronger protection than vaccination against emerging variants. title: Global burden of type 2 diabetes attributable to SARS-CoV-2 infection

analysis.scope_and_question: Objective We aimed to quantify the association between severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection and the risk of incident diabetes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies identified through PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and CENTRAL from inception to 29 January 2026. analysis.summary_en: This review quantifies the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and the risk of incident type 2 diabetes (T2D). title: Immune parameters in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during SARS-CoV2 delta and omicron waves.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Understanding immune mechanisms associated with COVID-19 severity remains important for interpreting clinical outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We investigated virological and immunological profiles in 39-patients hospitalized with COVID-19 at InCor Hospital during the Delta and Omicron waves and included 28-non-hospitalized individuals with moderate COVID-19 as a comparator group for cytokine analyses.
analysis.methods: SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed by RT-PCR from nasopharyngeal swabs, and viral variants were identified by next-generation sequencing. RNAemia was assessed by RT-PCR and analyzed as a binary variable. Serum cytokines were quantified by cytometric bead array, while humoral responses were evaluated by anti-Spike RBD IgG levels using CLIA and a Wuhan-Hu-1-based pseudovirus neutralization assay.
analysis.main_results: Cytokine profiling showed increased IL-6, IL-8, TNF, IL-17 A and IL-10 levels in hospitalized patients compared with moderate COVID-19 individuals, but did not distinguish recovered from deceased patients. Neutralizing antibody titers measured against a Wuhan-Hu-1 spike pseudovirus were significantly higher in recovered individuals than decease patients, underscoring the relevance of antibody functionality.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These data emphasize the relevance of viral dissemination and functional humoral immunity as potential biomarkers for COVID-19 progression and outcome, with RNAemia and neutralizing antibody levels showing a stronger exploratory association in this cohort.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: RNAemia and neutralizing antibody levels may serve as biomarkers for COVID-19 progression and outcome, highlighting the importance of viral dissemination and functional humoral immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the small sample size and the absence of a randomized control group, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated virological and immunological profiles in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during the Delta and Omicron waves, showing increased cytokine levels and higher neutralizing antibody titers in recovered individuals compared to deceased patients. The findings suggest RNAemia and neutralizing antibody levels as potential biomarkers for disease progression and outcome.

title: Impact of Community Factors on Mental and Physical Health During Successive Waves of COVID-19 Pandemic in China.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study examined how community factors impacted well-being during the COVID-19 pandemic in China.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Data were collected at two time points: Time 1 (T1) in September 2021 (N = 992) when COVID-19 cases stabilized, and Time 2 (T2) in January 2023 (N = 497) during a sudden outbreak of new infected cases.
analysis.methods: At T1, perceived community safety and sense of community directly affected depression, anxiety, and physical health symptoms, with sense of community partially mediating these effects.
analysis.main_results: At T2, community factors at T1 continued to impact depression, anxiety, and physical health symptoms.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Sense of community at T1 partially mediated the link between community safety at T1 and mental health at T2.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Higher income and older age were associated with a stronger sense of community, better perceived community safety, and improved health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Policymakers should consider the impact of community factors on well-being during health crises.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of community factors on mental and physical health during successive waves of the COVID-19 pandemic in China. Data were collected at two time points: September 2021 (N = 992) when cases stabilized and January 2023 (N = 497) during a sudden outbreak. The findings showed that community factors at the first time point continued to influence mental and physical health at the second time point. Specifically, sense of community at T1 partially mediated the relationship between community safety at T1 and mental health at T2. Higher income and older age were linked to better community safety and improved health outcomes. The study highlights the importance of community factors in shaping well-being during health crises and suggests that policymakers should consider these factors in their strategies. The evidence is based on data collected from two time points, and the study provides insights into the long-term effects of community dynamics on health outcomes.

title: Association between COVID-19 vaccination, SARS-CoV-2 infection, and oral lichen planus (OLP) flares: Results from a patient survey

analysis.scope_and_question: The study aimed to explore the association with an increased occurrence of OLP flares following COVID-19 vaccination or infection. Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic immune-mediated mucocutaneous disease. During the COVID-19 pandemic, new cases and flares of OLP were reported after SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: An 11-question survey was distributed to OLP patients. Associations with complications were assessed with Fisher's exact or Wilcoxon tests.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Overall, OLP flares were not reported at high rates with COVID-19 vaccination or infection. Within these limitations, the findings of the study suggest that participants who experience systemic side effects following a COVID-19 vaccine may be more susceptible to OLP flares.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study reports that self-reported OLP flares were significantly associated with whether or not participants also reported vaccine side effects (p = 0.005). However, the evidence is limited and based on self-reporting, which may introduce bias. The study also found that experiencing systemic side effects following the 2nd vaccination was again significantly associated with reporting an OLP flare (p = 0.048).
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Clarifying this relationship is important for improving patient counseling and management during vaccination efforts. Experiencing an OLP flare following the 1st COVID-19 vaccination was significantly associated with experiencing a flare again after receiving the 2nd vaccination.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination and oral lichen planus (OLP) flares through a survey of 76 OLP patients. It reports that 20% of participants experienced OLP flares after vaccination, and 33% after infection. Self-reported OLP flares were significantly linked to vaccine side effects (p = 0.005), with 37% of those reporting systemic side effects also experiencing flares compared to 8% without side effects. A second dose of the vaccine was associated with 21% of participants reporting flares. The study concludes that OLP flares are not commonly reported with vaccination or infection, but those experiencing systemic side effects may be more susceptible. The findings highlight the need for improved patient counseling and management during vaccination efforts, and suggest further research into the relationship between vaccine-induced immune responses and OLP flares.

title: Severity-dependent and sex-biased dysregulation of A-to-I RNA editing in COVID-19 reveals CTSS as a key regulatory target

analysis.research_question_and_background: SARS-CoV-2 infection causes diverse clinical outcomes, with men facing higher risks of severe disease. Adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing mediated by ADAR enzymes governs innate antiviral immunity, yet its contribution to COVID-19 severity and sex-biased disease remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We performed epitranscriptomic profiling on 126 blood samples from non-COVID controls and COVID-19 patients spanning different disease severities. The study included patients with varying levels of disease severity, including ICU patients, and compared them with non-ICU patients.
analysis.methods: We detected 1,466 differentially RNA-edited sites in 514 genes linked to clinical outcomes. The study involved epitranscriptomic profiling of blood samples to identify RNA editing patterns associated with disease severity and sex differences.
analysis.main_results: Although ADAR expression increased in COVID-19 patients overall, it was strongly reduced in ICU patients compared with non-ICU patients, and this shift was far more prominent in males. This severity-associated and sex-biased ADAR/ADARB1 downregulation coincided with decreased global RNA editing and perturbed expression of immune-related edited transcripts.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Cathepsin S (CTSS) was identified as a central regulatory node: elevated A-to-I editing within its 3’ UTR in ICU patients stabilizes CTSS mRNA. This indicates severity-dependent, not infection-innate, disruption of A-to-I editing, disproportionately amplified in critically ill males.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: CTSS 3’UTR editing may serve as a biomarker for patient stratification, revealing a mechanistic connection between epitranscriptomic changes and male-biased severe COVID-19.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Without stratifying by disease severity, ADAR expression and global editing showed no significant sex differences; the large sex divergence only appeared among ICU patients. The evidence is moderate as it is based on abstract-only data and does not provide detailed statistical or methodological validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of A-to-I RNA editing in SARS-CoV-2 infection, focusing on its association with disease severity and sex differences. The research highlights that ADAR expression and RNA editing are significantly reduced in ICU patients, particularly in males, and identifies CTSS as a key regulatory target. These findings suggest a potential biomarker for patient stratification and a mechanistic link between epitranscriptomic changes and male-biased severe outcomes. However, the study's evidence is moderate due to its reliance on abstract-only data and the lack of detailed statistical analysis.

title: Administrative Primacy as an Interpretive Framework for Health System Governance: A Document-Based Analysis of Three Publicly Reported Episodes During the 2021 Fujian COVID-19 Outbreak Response

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the governance of the 2021 Fujian Delta variant outbreak of SARS-CoV-2, examining how administrative performance metrics may influence clinical judgment and ethical reasoning during public health emergencies. The central question is whether administrative primacy can be identified as a pattern in health system governance during such crises.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review employs a document-based ethical case analysis using publicly available sources: official government communications, state-approved media reports, and peer-reviewed literature. A Poisson incidence density model was used as an auxiliary sensitivity analysis to evaluate the plausibility of reported occupational outcomes. All cited documentary sources are publicly accessible and independently retrievable.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Three domains of concern were identified, each supported by documentary sources, including official documents and media reports. These episodes are consistent with the Administrative Primacy framework, which suggests that administrative performance metrics may, in some circumstances, conflict with clinical ethics, occupational protection norms, and institutional transparency.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The overnight mobilisation of 320 pre-licensure medical students for high-frequency nasopharyngeal sampling raised occupational safety and consent concerns. The reported zero-infection outcome was lower than expected under comparator assumptions, prompting a need for verification. Additionally, the framework is presented as a hypothesis rather than an established policy gap.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The framework is offered as a replicable analytical tool for evaluating governance-ethics alignment in future emergency responses. Three domains are identified as candidate areas for further health-system governance review, framed as hypotheses generated by this single case.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the 2021 Fujian Delta variant outbreak of SARS-CoV-2 through the lens of Administrative Primacy, a framework highlighting how administrative performance metrics may influence clinical judgment and ethical reasoning. Three episodes are analyzed: a pediatric CT case involving regulatory and ethical concerns, the mobilization of medical students for sampling with safety and consent issues, and a hospital administrative exception linked to ICU closure. The review identifies these as potential illustrations of governance patterns where administrative priorities may conflict with clinical ethics and occupational norms. While the framework is presented as a hypothesis for future governance review, the study underscores the need for verification of reported outcomes and the importance of aligning administrative practices with ethical standards during public health emergencies.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Live Attenuated COVID-19 Vaccine Candidate Based on Omicron-like Temperature-Sensitive Mutant in Preclinical Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has ended, emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants remain a future threat.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of an intranasal live attenuated vaccine (LAV) prototype based on a temperature-sensitive (ts) Omicron-like SARS-CoV-2 mutant in a Syrian hamster COVID-19 model.
analysis.methods: SARS-CoV-2 Dubrovka (Wuhan-like), Otradnoe (BA.1.1) and FEB2 (BA.5.2) strains and the ts F-F3 mutant derived from FEB2 were characterized by electron microscopy, nanopore sequencing, cytopathic effect titration, and RT-PCR. In vitro studies used Vero CCL-81 cells; in vivo transmissibility and efficacy studies were assessed in female Syrian hamsters. Serum antibody titers were measured by ELISA and neutralization assays. Immunization efficacy was assessed by weight change; viral loads in the lungs, nasal passages, and brain; and histological examination of the lungs at day 4 post-challenge.
analysis.main_results: The F-F3 strain displayed a stable ts phenotype in vitro, did not infect hamster lungs or brain, and showed no transmission from immunized to naïve co-housed animals. A single intranasal immunization by F-F3 induced seroconversion, reduced pneumonia severity by 76.2% and 79.5% in two independent experiments (p < 0.01), protected the lungs against productive infection while reducing viral load in the nasal passages, and resulted in no detectable viral transmission after homologous BA.5.2 challenge. Following heterologous Wuhan-like challenge, immunization prevented weight loss and significantly reduced viral loads in the lungs, nasal passages, and brain; however, protection against pneumonia was only modest (18.6%; p < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Preclinical evaluation of the F-F3-based LAV prototype demonstrated a favorable balance between safety and efficacy. These characteristics support its further consideration as a candidate strain for COVID-19 LAV development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the F-F3-based LAV could be a promising candidate for further development in the context of emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants, particularly for its safety profile and efficacy against homologous challenges.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to preclinical evaluation in a Syrian hamster model, which may not fully represent human immune responses. The evidence is moderate as it is based on in vitro and in vivo studies without human trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of an intranasal live attenuated vaccine (LAV) candidate based on a temperature-sensitive (ts) Omicron-like SARS-CoV-2 mutant in a Syrian hamster model. The F-F3 strain was characterized using electron microscopy, nanopore sequencing, cytopathic effect titration, and RT-PCR. In vitro studies were conducted on Vero CCL-81 cells, while in vivo studies assessed transmissibility and efficacy in female hamsters. The vaccine induced seroconversion and significantly reduced pneumonia severity (76.2% and 79.5% in two experiments, p < 0.01) and viral loads in the nasal passages. It showed no transmission after homologous BA.5.2 challenge. However, protection against heterologous Wuhan-like challenge was modest (18.6%; p < 0.05). The preclinical results suggest a favorable safety and efficacy balance, supporting further development of the F-F3-based LAV. The study is limited to animal models and lacks human trials, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Association of In-Hospital Antimalarial–Macrolide Therapy With 3–6-Month Cardiac Electrophysiological Outcomes in Survivors of Severe COVID-19: A Matched Retrospective Cohort Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the cardiac electrophysiological outcomes of survivors of severe COVID-19 pneumonia 3–6 months after hospitalization and compare these outcomes based on exposure to combined antimalarial–macrolide therapy. The background highlights concerns about the potential cardiac effects of these drugs, particularly their ability to prolong ventricular repolarization and increase arrhythmia risk.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective matched cohort study was conducted involving adults hospitalized for severe COVID-19 pneumonia between March and June 2020. Patients exposed to hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine in combination with azithromycin or clarithromycin were matched 1:1 with patients who did not receive either drug class based on sex and age (±3 years).
analysis.methods: Cardiovascular assessments 3–6 months post-hospitalization included 12-lead electrocardiograms and 24-hour Holter monitoring. The study evaluated QTc intervals, conduction abnormalities, arrhythmias, and heart rate variability (HRV).
analysis.main_results: Eighty-six patients were included (43 exposed and 43 unexposed). Follow-up QTc intervals were similar between groups (420.0 vs. 423.1 ms; p = 0.762), and QTc prolongation was uncommon. No malignant ventricular arrhythmias or clinically significant conduction abnormalities were identified. Exposed patients had a higher prevalence of sinus bradycardia, a lower resting heart rate on electrocardiography, and higher HRV as assessed by the standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that short-term in-hospital exposure to combined antimalarial–macrolide therapy was not associated with persistent QTc prolongation or clinically significant electrophysiological abnormalities at 3–6 months. This study provides novel insights into post-recovery cardiac outcomes in severe COVID-19 survivors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that combined antimalarial–macrolide therapy during hospitalization for severe COVID-19 may not have long-term cardiac electrophysiological consequences, which could inform future treatment strategies and risk assessments for patients recovering from severe infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study notes that differences in heart rate and HRV should be interpreted cautiously due to potential residual confounding from acute disease severity. The evidence is moderate, as the study is retrospective and relies on observational data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the cardiac electrophysiological outcomes of survivors of severe COVID-19 pneumonia 3–6 months after hospitalization, comparing those exposed to combined antimalarial–macrolide therapy with unexposed patients. The retrospective matched cohort design included 86 patients (43 exposed and 43 unexposed) hospitalized between March and June 2020. Cardiovascular assessments involved 12-lead electrocardiograms and 24-hour Holter monitoring, evaluating QTc intervals, conduction abnormalities, arrhythmias, and heart rate variability (HRV). Results showed similar follow-up QTc intervals between groups, with no malignant ventricular arrhythmias or clinically significant conduction abnormalities identified. Exposed patients had a higher prevalence of sinus bradycardia, lower resting heart rate, and higher HRV. The authors concluded that short-term in-hospital exposure to combined antimalarial–macrolide therapy was not associated with persistent QTc prolongation or clinically significant electrophysiological abnormalities. However, the study acknowledges limitations due to potential residual confounding from acute disease severity, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: From past to present and toward the future: a mechanism-informed clinical framework for COVID-19-associated headache and post-viral pain

analysis.scope_and_question: Headache is a prominent acute and persistent neurological manifestation of COVID-19, representing both as a significant clinical challenge and a valuable model for understanding the neurotropic effects of SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This review synthesizes evidence showing that the epidemiology of COVID-19 headache is distinctly shaped by younger age, female sex, and a prior history of headache disorders; its clinical phenotypes are diverse, strongly associating with chemosensory dysfunctions such as anosmia; and its core pathophysiology involves neuroinflammation (e.g., cytokine-mediated pathways), trigeminovascular activation, and sex-specific neuroendocrine-immune interactions.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Although acute headache often responds to conventional analgesics, persistent cases—a major component of Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC)—necessitate a multidisciplinary management approach.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: This contrasts with the typically self-limiting headache following vaccination.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize longitudinal studies to define chronicity, mechanistic investigations into sex-specific pathways, and the development of phenotype-specific, personalized therapeutic strategies.

The study highlights that headache is more prevalent in younger individuals, females, and those with a history of headache disorders, and is strongly linked to chemosensory dysfunctions like anosmia. The core mechanisms involve neuroinflammation, trigeminovascular activation, and sex-specific neuroendocrine-immune interactions. While acute headaches may respond to standard analgesics, persistent cases, particularly those linked to Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), require a multidisciplinary approach. The article notes that headache following vaccination is typically self-limiting, contrasting with the chronic nature of post-COVID headaches. It concludes by advocating for future research to focus on longitudinal studies, sex-specific mechanisms, and personalized therapeutic strategies for managing persistent post-COVID headaches.

title: COVID-19 vaccination and survival of cancer patients in Northwestern Russia: a historical registry-based cohort study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cancer patients face a significantly elevated risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes, and data on vaccination coverage and its association with survival among Russian cancer patients remain scarce.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This historical registry-based cohort study integrated data from the Population-Based Cancer Registry (PBCR) of the Arkhangelsk Region and the Nenets Autonomous Okrug, regional vaccination records, and an artificial intelligence (AI)-based analysis of chest computed tomography (CT) scans. The cohort consisted of 1,144 cancer patients who underwent CT between August 2020 and April 2021.
analysis.methods: Overall survival (OS) was compared between vaccinated and unvaccinated patients using Kaplan–Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusted for demographic, clinical, and AI-derived CT biomarkers. Vaccination status was ascertained via data linkage and defined as receipt of at least one dose before the landmark date.
analysis.main_results: Only 6.6% (n=76) of patients received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine (Sputnik V or Sputnik Light). In the primary landmark analysis, vaccination was associated with a significantly higher 3-year OS (80.3% vs. 68.7% for unvaccinated patients). In multivariable analysis, vaccination was independently associated with a 60% lower hazard of all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.25–0.64).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Vaccination was strongly associated with a substantial survival benefit, underscoring its importance as a potentially lifesaving intervention for this vulnerable population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the critical need to improve vaccination coverage among cancer patients in Northwest Russia and inform targeted public health strategies to enhance survival outcomes in this high-risk group.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential immortal time bias, which was mitigated using a landmark approach. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on registry data and the absence of randomized controlled trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between COVID-19 vaccination and survival in cancer patients in Northwest Russia. It reveals critically low vaccination coverage among this vulnerable population, with vaccinated patients showing a 60% lower hazard of all-cause mortality compared to unvaccinated patients. The study uses a historical registry-based cohort design, integrating data from cancer registries, vaccination records, and AI analysis of CT scans. The findings suggest that vaccination may offer a substantial survival benefit, emphasizing its importance for cancer patients. The results have implications for improving vaccination rates and public health strategies in this region.

title: Municipality-level ecological analysis of COVID-19 mortality and infections in Austria, 2020 to 2023

analysis.research_question_and_background: Previous studies indicated that regional fluctuations in COVID-19 impact were associated with socioeconomic, demographic and environmental factors early in the pandemic. It is unclear whether factors associated with regional COVID-19 mortality and SARS-CoV-2 infections changed over the course of the pandemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We evaluated the association of ecological factors with municipality-specific COVID-19 mortality in the national population of Austria between January 2020 and June 2023. Analyses were conducted separately per calendar year and pooled across years via random-effects meta-analysis.
analysis.methods: Outcomes were analysed using univariable and multivariable zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression, including annually averaged environmental exposome exposure (including air pollution and UV radiation), socioeconomic, demographic and infection dissemination predictors with significance threshold set to p<0.005. Secondary analysis modelled SARS-CoV-2 infections using of negative-binomial model (NB). Two additional approaches for smaller predictor set selection were applied as sensitivity analyses.
analysis.main_results: Within the entire observation period 18,430 COVID-19 deaths were reported. In univariable analyses (pooled RR (99.5% CI)), COVID-19 mortality was significantly associated with the proportion of commuters (0.79 (0.73-0.86)), residents aged 75-84 (1.18 (1.01-1.37)) and [≥]85 years (1.29 (1.04-1.60)), residents with at most compulsory education (1.15 (1.02-1.29)), employed residents aged 15-64 (0.89 (0.85-0.93)), and homeowners (0.91 (0.83-0.99)), as well as with precipitation (0.94 (0.89-0.99)) and the average time with a mean temperature of 5-15 C (0.95 (0.90-0.99)). In multivariable analyses the share of population aged 85 or older (1.30 (1.09-1.54)) and home ownership (0.92 (0.87-0.98)) were independently significant.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Throughout the pandemic in Austria, demographic and socioeconomic factors were associated with COVID-19 mortality and infections, but many associations, especially for infections, were unstable over time. These findings underscore the importance of structural vulnerabilities in epidemic impact.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that demographic and socioeconomic factors play a role in the impact of SARS-CoV-2 in Austria, highlighting the need for targeted public health interventions. They also indicate that the stability of these associations over time may inform future surveillance and prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its ecological design, which may obscure individual-level variability. The evidence is moderate as the findings are based on pooled analyses and associations rather than causal relationships.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted an ecological analysis of SARS-CoV-2 mortality and infections at the municipality level in Austria from 2020 to 2023. It aimed to assess whether factors influencing regional impacts of the pandemic changed over time. The study used zero-inflated negative binomial regression and random-effects meta-analysis to evaluate associations between ecological factors, socioeconomic variables, and demographic characteristics with mortality and infections. Results showed that factors such as age distribution, employment status, and housing conditions were significantly associated with mortality, while some variables, like air pollution and overnight stays, had mixed effects. The authors concluded that demographic and socioeconomic factors remained important throughout the pandemic, but associations for infections were unstable over time. The study's ecological design limits the strength of its conclusions, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the nature of the associations observed.

title: Pentosan polysulfate sodium limits pulmonary inflammation in a SARS-CoV-2 mouse model

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the urgent need for effective therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2-induced severe pulmonary inflammation and mortality, given the ongoing global prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 infections and the limited availability of specific antiviral treatments.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized the K18-hACE2 mouse model of SARS-CoV-2 infection, administering pentosan polysulfate sodium (PPS) via intranasal instillation at early (1 day post-infection) or late (3 days post-infection) stages to evaluate its efficacy in mitigating viral-induced inflammation and disease outcomes.
analysis.methods: PPS was administered at 6 mg/kg from either 1 or 3 days post-infection. The study examined weight loss, clinical disease presentation, neutrophilic airway inflammation, pro-inflammatory cytokine production, viral titers, and interferon and antiviral gene expression through histological and molecular analyses.
analysis.main_results: Early PPS administration significantly improved weight loss, clinical disease presentation, and reduced neutrophilic airway inflammation and pro-inflammatory cytokine production. Late PPS administration worsened weight loss and clinical disease presentation, and increased pro-inflammatory cytokine production and downregulated antiviral-associated genes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the importance of timing in PPS administration for its therapeutic efficacy against SARS-CoV-2-induced inflammation, demonstrating its potential as a repurposed anti-inflammatory agent.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study underscores the significance of time-dependent administration of PPS for mitigating SARS-CoV-2-induced pulmonary inflammation and tissue remodeling, suggesting its potential for clinical implementation in treating severe COVID-19 cases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a mouse model, which may not fully represent human responses, and the lack of direct comparison with other antiviral treatments. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of human clinical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the efficacy of pentosan polysulfate sodium (PPS) in mitigating SARS-CoV-2-induced pulmonary inflammation in a mouse model. Early PPS administration significantly improved disease outcomes, while late administration worsened them, highlighting the importance of timing for therapeutic efficacy.

title: Crystal structures of the N-terminal and C-terminal domains of the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to elucidate the structural features of the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein, particularly its roles in RNA binding, genome packaging and ribonucleoprotein (RNP) assembly.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved determining crystal structures of the N-terminal domain (NTD) and C-terminal domain (CTD) of the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein. Structures were obtained from crystals grown at different pH levels and resolutions.
analysis.methods: Crystal structures of the NTD and CTD were determined using X-ray crystallography. The NTD was analyzed at pH 8.0 with a resolution of 1.94 Å, while the CTD was analyzed at pH 5.0 and 8.5 with resolutions of 1.59 and 1.30 Å, respectively.
analysis.main_results: Comparison of the apo NTD structure with a previously reported RNA-bound NTD structure revealed local differences in the side-chain conformations of RNA-contacting residues, including Thr49, Arg88, Arg92, Arg107, Tyr109 and Tyr111, while the overall domain fold remained essentially unchanged. The CTD forms a domain-swapped dimer mediated by β-hairpins, with a positively charged groove extending across the dimer interface. Superposition of the two CTD structures yielded a root-mean-square deviation (r.m.s.d.) of 0.129 Å, and 11 intersubunit hydrogen bonds were observed at the dimer interface in each structure.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that RNA binding may be accommodated by local side-chain rearrangements within a pre-existing positively charged cleft rather than by a large-scale conformational change. These structures provide a framework for further investigation of NTD-RNA recognition and the possible role of the CTD positively charged groove in nucleic acid interactions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The structures offer insights into the molecular mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein function, which could inform future studies on viral RNA interactions and the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to structural analysis and does not include functional or clinical data. The evidence is strong as it provides detailed structural insights based on high-resolution crystallography.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents the crystal structures of the N-terminal and C-terminal domains of the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein, revealing structural features relevant to RNA binding and dimer formation. The NTD structure shows local side-chain differences in RNA-contacting residues, while the CTD forms a conserved dimer with a positively charged groove. These findings provide a structural basis for understanding N-protein interactions and assembly, which could guide future research on viral mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets. The study is limited to structural analysis and does not include functional or clinical data, but the evidence is strong due to the high-resolution crystallography used.

title: A mosaic RBD-nanoparticle pan-sarbecovirus vaccine elicits nanobodies that target highly conserved epitopes

analysis.research_question_and_background: SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, continually mutates, producing new variants of concern (VOCs). Substitutions in the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein receptor-binding domain (RBD) have resulted in reduced efficacies of vaccines and therapeutic monoclonal antibodies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: To address VOC substitutions effects on therapeutic antibody efficacy, we sought to identify single-domain nanobodies (VHHs) targeting RBD regions (class 4, class 1/4, portions of class 3 and class 5 RBD epitopes) that are more conserved across VOCs.
analysis.methods: We used a Beacon optofluidic platform to isolate and characterize single memory B cells from a llama immunized with a mosaic RBD-nanoparticle immunogen that elicits broad antibody responses across sarbecoviruses.
analysis.main_results: Using multiplex binding assays, we identified nanobodies that bind to spike RBDs from diverse sarbecovirus strains. title: Presence of post-COVID-19 condition in six ethnic groups in Amsterdam, the Netherlands: a retrospectively reconstructed time interval approach.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) and its determinants among six ethnic groups in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, to address the knowledge gap regarding ethnic disparities in long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from participants in the HELIUS cohort who had SARS-CoV-2 infection and answered questions about COVID-19-related symptoms between May and November 2022. The study included 932 infected participants.
analysis.methods: The prevalence of PCC was estimated by ethnicity at several timepoints since infection, adjusted for age and sex. Logistic regression was used to assess determinants of PCC overall.
analysis.main_results: Of 932 infected participants, 31% [95% confidence interval (95%CI): 27%–37%] developed PCC. At 3 months after infection, the adjusted prevalence of PCC varied from 17% (95%CI: 13%–24%) in the Dutch-origin group to 41% (95%CI: 34%–48%) in the South-Asian Surinamese group.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal significant ethnic differences in PCC prevalence, with South-Asian Surinamese, Turkish, and Moroccan participants showing higher rates compared to Dutch participants, highlighting the need for targeted research and interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform public health strategies for surveillance and management of post-COVID-19 conditions, particularly in ethnic minority populations, and suggest the importance of considering sociodemographic factors in future studies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on self-reported symptoms, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations and the potential for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) among six ethnic groups in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, using a retrospective cohort approach. It found that 31% of 932 infected participants developed PCC, with significant variations by ethnicity. South-Asian Surinamese, Turkish, and Moroccan individuals had higher adjusted prevalence rates compared to Dutch participants. The study highlights ethnic disparities in PCC and suggests the need for targeted public health strategies. However, the retrospective design and reliance on self-reported symptoms limit the confidence in the findings, resulting in a moderate evidence assessment.

title: Glycemic dysregulation and insulin resistance across acute and post-acute COVID-19: a systematic review and meta-analysis of etiologic and prognostic evidence

analysis.scope_and_question: The review aims to synthesize evidence on glycemic dysregulation and insulin resistance or insulin sensitivity across acute and post-acute COVID-19, including metabolic trajectories and associations with adverse clinical outcomes. The topic boundary includes SARS-CoV-2, COVID-19, and named SARS-CoV-2 variants, with species-level Betacoronavirus pandemicum qualified as it includes related viruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect were searched. Eligible studies evaluated glucose regulation and at least one insulin-resistance or insulin-sensitivity measure during or after COVID-19. Etiological and prognostic evidence were analyzed as related but distinct domains. Prognostic meta-analysis evaluated study-defined acute hyperglycemic phenotypes; insulin-resistance or insulin-sensitivity assessment was a study-level eligibility criterion rather than part of a participant-level composite exposure. Risk of bias was assessed using design-appropriate tools, and certainty was evaluated with GRADE. The protocol and analytical plan were retrospectively registered in OSF on August 21, 2026.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Acute hyperglycemic phenotypes were associated with increased short-term all-cause mortality (four studies; 1,079 participants; RR 2.09, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.21–3.64; I 2 =31.3%; 95% prediction interval 0.96–4.56) and invasive mechanical ventilation (three studies; 679 participants; RR 3.64, 95% CI 1.74–7.61; I 2 =0%). Mortality estimates remained directionally stable in sensitivity analysis. Etiological evidence showed no uniform post-COVID trajectory: insulin resistance or glycemic abnormalities resolved in some populations, persisted in others, and progressed toward newly diagnosed diabetes in a subset.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Adding a large study using peak in-hospital glucose preserved the mortality association but produced substantial heterogeneity for ventilation. The review notes that these unadjusted estimates should not be interpreted as effects of a combined phenotype or as causal associations. Persistent metabolic abnormalities occurred heterogeneously, supporting standardized participant-level definitions and controlled longitudinal studies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for standardized participant-level definitions and controlled longitudinal studies to better understand the trajectory of metabolic abnormalities post-COVID-19.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis explores glycemic dysregulation and insulin resistance or sensitivity across acute and post-acute COVID-19, focusing on metabolic trajectories and associations with adverse outcomes. The review included 23 reports from 20 independent studies, with meta-analyses on acute hyperglycemic phenotypes linked to increased short-term mortality and mechanical ventilation. Mortality estimates remained stable in sensitivity analyses, while etiological evidence showed varied post-COVID metabolic outcomes. The study highlights the need for standardized participant-level definitions and controlled longitudinal research to better understand these metabolic changes. The review also notes limitations, including heterogeneity in ventilation outcomes and the need to avoid interpreting unadjusted estimates as causal effects.
